properties.name: MEASURED (flo2's 0.83.5 move, way-back test): after a 0.83.4 writes into a store that 0.83.5 stamped, 0.83.5's one-shot --call does not rebuild the search index and misses words in prose fields. The stamp (fulltext/built-under.json) still names 0.83.5's field list. A 0.83.5 server is not affected
properties.statement:
The known limit named in chg:search-reads-every-prose-field-2026-10-13, now measured. Measured by flo2's 0.83.5 move agent on a copy of flo2's design (2,045 nodes), with both published binaries:
1. 0.83.5 opened the store: it rebuilt once, wrote built-under.json, and found three words that only a change's rationale holds.
2. 0.83.4 then wrote a change into the store (indexed with 0.83.4's fields only), and a 0.83.4 server opened it (rebuilding the whole index with 0.83.4's fields). built-under.json was left untouched, still naming 0.83.5's list.
3. 0.83.5 through --call: no rebuild. It missed the rationale of the change 0.83.4 wrote, and also "misdiagnosed", a word in an older change's rationale.
4. A 0.83.5 server found both, because a server rebuilds at every start. So flo2.io is unaffected.
WHAT IT TAKES: going back to an older reflow2 and forward again on one store, with only the --call door after. A fix would have to stamp the index with WHO last wrote it (or have every write bump a counter the stamp records), because an older binary cannot be taught to update the stamp. Not root-caused further; recorded as a to-do (rule:a-reflow2-tool-failure-met-while-working-is-captured-as-a-to-do). Logs: the move agent's wayback.log.
